Looking at the first fold: the crease AB makes angle α = 63° with the strip's edges. Folding along AB turns the straight strip into a "∧" shape; the angle between the two arms of the ∧ is 180° − 2α = 180° − 126° = 54°.

For the second fold, the crease runs along the edge of one arm (parallel to that arm). Reflecting the other arm across this crease preserves the angle it makes with the crease direction. Since the crease is parallel to the remaining arm, the angle β between the twice-folded arm and the remaining arm equals the apex angle of the ∧:

β = 180° − 2α = 180° − 2(63°) = 54°.

\boxed{D}
